script: John McAfee wrote one of the first antivirus programs in 1987 and gave it away for free. He wasn't being generous, he was building the market. Every time a new virus appeared and his software caught it, his mailing list grew. By 1992, McAfee Associates was a public company. McAfee sold his stake and left two years later with roughly $100 million and no interest in running a software business. Until Intel bought the company he'd founded for $7.68 billion in 2010, McAfee was not involved. By then, he had moved to Belize, was running a compound with armed guards, and claimed to be manufacturing illegal antibiotics. In 2012, his neighbor was shot and killed. McAfee was named a person of interest. He fled through the jungle, live-blogging his escape, sought asylum in Guatemala, was deported, and surfaced in the US claiming innocence. He ran for president twice, was indicted for tax evasion, and was arrested in Spain in 2020. From a Spanish prison cell in 2021, he tweeted that if he was ever found dead, it would not be suicide. Three months later, he was found dead in that cell. It was ruled a suicide. The company still carries his name.
retention_tricks: Rapid stick-figure animation paired with real photos and cutouts
Escalating story rhythm filled with shocking real-life events
Conspiracy twist near the end using his actual famous tweet screenshot
what_makes_it_work: Humorous stick-figure cutout aesthetic simplifies complex historical narratives into bitesize comic beats.
Incredible escalation from software engineer to international fugitive keeps viewer curiosity high throughout.
Strong payoff landing on his conspiracy tweet right before his mysterious death.
